title: Permission traffic simulator and golden-state assertion suite
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build a reproducible test harness that replays representative permission check traffic (from anonymized audit logs and synthetic SSO flows) to generate canonical 'golden-state' permission matrices and run deterministic assertions across RBAC v2 runtime variants. Goal is catch regressions introduced by kernel scheduling, caching changes, or permission evaluation refactors before release.
acceptance_criteria:
- A traffic simulator that can replay 1M permission checks/day locally and in CI (scaled down).
- Golden-state generation pipeline that emits compact assertions (JSON lines) and a signed hash for verification.
- CI job that compares current run to golden-state and blocks PRs on non-exempt diffs.
- Test coverage for edge cases: expired session tokens, SAML role mapping changes, nested resource scoping, wildcard permissions.
- Documentation and runbook for regenerating goldens and triaging failures.
test_plan:
1) Ingest anonymized audit log snippets stored in s3://redwood-testdata/rbac-samples/; 2) Run simulator to produce permission-check traces with identity, session attributes, and resource context; 3) Apply current RBAC v2 evaluator and collect per-check outcomes; 4) Collapse outcomes into golden assertions grouped by role-set + resource-pattern; 5) Store goldens in the golden registry (versioned) and publish hash to CI.
We will include a parallel pipeline that runs against the 'canary' runtime images built by CI to compare behavior under kernel/quantization changes.
ci_integration: Create a CircleCI workflow (or reuse existing runner) that executes the simulator at PR-level for changed files in rbac/ and runtime/ directories with a lightweight sample set; schedule nightly full-run comparing against full golden set. Block merges on non-trivial assertion diffs; allow opt-in 'regeneration' flow requiring approval from Security and Platform leads. See .circleci/config.yml#rbac-golden for proposed job names.
metrics_to_track:
- False-positive rate (number of assertion diffs triaged as non-bugs)
- Time to triage (median) for golden diffs
- CI runtime for PR-level run (target < 10 minutes)
- % coverage of permission patterns (target 95% of observed production patterns)
- Number of regressions caught pre-release
implementation_notes: We will implement the simulator in Go (reuse internal rbac-client libraries) to get parity with runtime types. Golden assertions will be stored as newline-delimited JSON with fields: role_set_id, resource_pattern, input_attributes_hash, allowed/denied counts, and rng-seed for nondeterministic cases. For determinism we will freeze RNG seeds for CBOR-marshalling order and normalise timestamps. Consider using merkle-like signed summary file to speed comparisons across large golden sets.
risk_and_mitigation:
Risk: Large golden sets can cause noisy CI and slow down PRs. Mitigation: PR-level sampling, nightly full-run, and hierarchical bucketing (shallow goldens for PRs, deep goldens for nightly).
Risk: Sensitive PII in production traces. Mitigation: strict anonymization pipeline and privacy review; only ingest pre-approved sanitized samples.
Risk: False positives from legitimate policy rollouts. Mitigation: regeneration workflow with audit trail and signed approvals.
tasks: Add CI jobs: pr-level-sim and nightly-full-compare
Write test vectors for SAML role mapping edge cases
notes: Initial spike showed 3 non-deterministic checks caused by timestamp handling in evaluator v1.2 — fixed by normalizing timestamps before hashing.
We decided to store goldens as compressed ndjson to enable line-by-line diffs in CI artifacts.
Security wants an approval label for any golden regen that increases allowance counts.
Discussed potential use of 'delta-ignore' rules to allow expected policy rollouts without blocking CI; to be finalized with PM and Security.
